[R896] POSITIVE - exact head 9a71daa9aa2379e2a57eb93ccafe83101bcb37f7

Independent external review, round R896-1, issue #973 / PR #978.
Tree: `0fe791d5c539f4100e312f17e469a2a9a50bc006`.
Reviewed range: `dd163e41..9a71daa9aa2379e2a57eb93ccafe83101bcb37f7`.

No BLOCKER, MAJOR, MINOR, RESIDUE or SUGGESTION was found. The scoped source change satisfies #973. This is a source-review verdict, not merge authorization or hardware qualification.

The independent assessment and ledger below were written before the public prior-finding reconciliation. No other reviewer's report was read.

## Contract and implementation

Read AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/README.md, [issue #973](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/973) and its TAKEN/REVIEW READY comments, REQUIREMENTS.md sections 1, 7 and 8, the SRP adapter contract, mailbox register/event-coalescing contracts, and the split control-memory ledger. The issue ties port lifecycle behavior to IEEE 802.1Q-2018 10.7 and 35.2. This verdict applies that existing project contract; it does not claim a fresh audit of every state-machine clause or full standards compliance.

The loop dispatches queued LINK records at `ctrl_loop.c:137-157`; the later SRP poll independently reads the current LINK register. The base poll could see a new UP before its record was dispatched. It reset the interface and set `link_seen`, making the eventual first LINK UP take the repeated-UP reset path. The host reproduction exposes both resets and startup-participant loss.

`srp_mbx.c:1231-1233` records the LINK value accepted by SRP's own sink. The poll at `:1284-1286` allows UP only while the carried level is UP, retaining the raw register's immediate DOWN. Attach initializes both levels from the same sample at `:1472-1474`. The existing reentry guard encloses these updates; no second state owner is introduced.

The first UP deliberately resets zero times, preserving already-clean participants; a subsequent UP after DOWN resets once. That implements the issue's startup-preservation intent, explicitly described in REVIEW READY. A repeated UP after prior activity remains meaningful for coalesced transitions and still resets.

The carried level intentionally survives `reset_interface`: when a raw DOWN's held record disappears on recovery, the last carried UP permits recovery. The existing `CancelledLinkRecordRecoversFromLevelAndFencesOldReceive` test checks this exception and old-input fencing. A dispatched DOWN does clear `link_carried`, preventing an early raw UP from starting an extra reset.

Other raw-level consumers were inspected: `adp/adp_mbx.c:44-47` supplies ADP's enable-time sample (`third_party/tsn-c-stack/src/adp.c:238`); subsequent transitions use LINK events. `maap/maap_mbx.c:273` samples at attach. Neither duplicates SRP's poll-time reset pattern. No mailbox ABI, timer, CDC, RTL, CPU bound, loop source or coverage ratchet changes in the reviewed range.

## Five-lens results

[R896] PASS Conformance - `sw/firmware/ctrl/srp/srp_mbx.c:1226`, `:1286`, `:1474`; #973 acceptance; `receipts/base-*.log`, `head-*.log` - confirmed the cause, startup preservation, single later-UP reset and retained fail-closed DOWN. Memory and CPU evidence below covers the other acceptance criteria without moving bounds.

[R896] PASS RTL - `sw/firmware/ctrl/srp/srp_mbx.h:68`; `srp_mbx.c:1160-1235`, `:1273-1319`; `loop/ctrl_loop.c:137-157`, `:289-331`; `docs/design/MAILBOX_SPLIT.md:182`; published platform-image comparisons - inspected serialization, interface indexing, attach/reset ownership, delayed rebuilding and dependent structure offsets. No RTL/crossing delta exists. Dependent objects reflect 8x8 structure-offset changes; published SRAM totals and tile allocations remain unchanged.

[R896] PASS Robustness - `sw/firmware/ctrl/test/srp_link_pass.cpp:77-135`; `srp_mbx.cpp:1004-1096`; `srp_app.cpp`; `receipts/head-8x8-2if.log` - exercised four UP phases, first/later UP, DOWN revocation, held-event recovery, reattach already UP, reentry refusal, malformed input, allocation/refusal paths and composition callbacks. Complete SRP mailbox/composition suites passed at both shipping shapes and 8x8/2if.

[R896] PASS Tests - `sw/firmware/ctrl/test/srp_link_pass.cpp:43-49`, `:87-135`; `srp_link_mutants.py:34-59`; `srp_mutants.py:19-34`, `:960-999`; `test_ctrl_firmware.py:212`, `:222-245`; `receipts/plants-*.log` - reset counting observes LICENCE writes independently of the participant-pointer check; outgoing declarations are also checked. Base fails in the intended diagnostic. All seven compiled plants fail the named assertion; compilation failures do not count as kills. Campaign wiring includes all three specified shapes.

[R896] PASS Docs - `sw/firmware/ctrl/srp/README.md:111-120`; `CHANGELOG.md:62-67`; public PR/issue evidence; `receipts/docs.log`, `em-dash.log`, `public-audit.log` - final behavior, attach exception and limits are documented. Added source comments describe behavior/reason and reference #973; no new bench label, lane name, review identity/round or issue-comment ID was found in them. Documentation gates pass.

## Reviewer execution

## Published source evidence

Source: [public packet at 62593bf0](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/tree/62593bf0adb29cb13e2f1ebaa95c76c496f5cdf0/review-evidence/973-r1/author-r1/receipts). `receipts/public-audit.log` identifies 28 examined artifacts and verifies their published SHA-256 values. Most gates ran at `862fd41cfc292d07480f0e6bb4b5dd5e0c42e2ea`. `git diff 862fd41c HEAD` confirms only a docstring rewrap follows: production bytes, test execution and mutation definitions are unchanged. Docs steps ran at the exact final head. Reviewer checks above ran at the exact final head.

The four firmware shard receipts report 77/77 suite verdicts, 826/826 control plants, 385 AECP and 564 SRP `[ok]` entries, zero escapes. These are selected gate output/summary receipts, not the full private campaign logs. Coverage self-test/check passes over 40 files. Twin, twin-plants, twin-maps and twin-maps-plants exit zero; the comparator reports zero findings, retaining documented placement differences. Final 8x8/1if ROM has 48 B before the next half-tile.

Published CPU runs cover ten groups at both points before/after, with zero refusals, budget misses or passes beyond the share. Independently parsed 88 paired 1x1 and 86 paired 8x8/1if probes: all fit, zero verdict changes, largest absolute rounded differences 0.438 ms and 0.146 ms. Independently rerun graders retain 1x1 load 0.511, last queued notice 127.31 ms, ACMP 29.06 ms, txL 47.88 ms; 8x8/1if load is 0.744 against 0.75. The latter point's reported analytic rows are not held bounds; measured rows are supported by the published CPU-run evidence.

## Prior public findings

After writing this verdict and ledger, read the PR conversation, formal reviews and inline review threads. The conversation contains the two manager review-start notices; formal reviews and inline threads are empty. There are no prior published findings on PR #978 to resolve or retain at this observation. ## Limits and pending manager duties

- A DOWN inside a pass can reset at the raw read and again at its record. This pre-existing, disclosed behavior precedes rebuilding and is outside #973's UP acceptance. No general exactly-one-reset claim for DOWN is approved.
- Illegal callback reentry can discard LINK; the existing guard counts/refuses it. No new delivery guarantee for unsupported reentry is claimed.
- [#970's ruling](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/970#issuecomment-7080789556) retains full ADP delay ranges. This head leaves ADP and the stack unchanged. [#972's manager decision](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/972#issuecomment-7083292610) requires effective link qualification from reset, beyond the arm's DOWN publication. #973 does not discharge that separate work. Its carried-level logic accepts the resulting DOWN/UP sequence; actual composed boot behavior needs candidate validation.
- Source baseline is the reviewed flip head `dd163e41`. No current-dev merge candidate was built here. The manager must validate the candidate against current dev, identified in the handoff as `e275d7950ef3385753e6a15d2e191ba855b171ed`, and publish exact-candidate builder/native receipts. Narrow ROM headroom makes composed image checks material.
- Hosted observation at this SHA found docs/elaborate in progress and rtl-fast/rtl-full queued. These are not successful contexts or executed exhaustive evidence. Hosted/act acceptance remains the manager's. No act, Docker, full parent/processor/synthesis/builder bank or hardware run was performed here.
- Physical calibration is NOT RUN. The builder's platform-specific skipped control and missing physical-report row do not prove the excluded measurements. Host tests, twin receipts and CPU simulation do not establish physical link, timing or audio behavior. The manager owns the bench rerun after merge.
- Merge still requires the other independent positive review, no round in flight, exact-candidate gates, required hosted acceptance, explicit authorization, containment, and issue/project completion.

[R895] NEGATIVE - exact head 9a71daa9aa2379e2a57eb93ccafe83101bcb37f7

Internal cleared-context independent review, round R895-1, issue #973 / PR #978.
Head `9a71daa9aa2379e2a57eb93ccafe83101bcb37f7`, tree `0fe791d5c539f4100e312f17e469a2a9a50bc006`.
Reviewed range: `dd163e41..9a71daa9` (the flip PR #960's reviewed head to the published head), eight commits.

This is a source-review verdict at one exact head. It is not merge authorization, not a manager source bank, and not hardware evidence.

## Verdict in one paragraph

The core fix is correct for the defect #973 describes. SRP's poll takes a DOWN from the LINK register and an UP only while the last LINK the loop dispatched carried one (`link_carried`). My own runs reproduce the defect on the base firmware at four shapes and show the head passing. All twelve planted defects are killed at 1x1/1if, 8x8/1if and 1x1/2if: the author's seven, the moved `srp-poll-extra-read`, and four of my own. The image ROM growth (+16 / +24 / +8 / +16 B, RAMB36 unchanged) reproduces at base and head. The loop and the coverage ratchet are byte-identical to the base.

The verdict is NEGATIVE for two reasons:
- **F1 (BLOCKER):** the new plant table is not registered with the firmware boundary gate. The hosted `firmware-boundary` job fails deterministically at this exact head. The author's validation never ran the documented local gate that would have caught it.
- **F2 (MINOR):** the fix adds a liveness regression on SRP's re-attach path. An executable probe shows it, and it falsifies a statement in the adapter README. The shipping boot path cannot reach it.

## Reconstruction

Read in order:
- `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` (merge bar, lenses, comment rules).
- `docs/README.md`.
- Issue #973: its body, frozen acceptance, TAKEN and REVIEW READY. There were no maintainer scope comments beyond those.
- Related issues #970 and #972.
- The authorities: `docs/reference/MAILBOX_CONTRACT.md` (LINK register `0x014`, LINK event), `hdl/milan/mailbox/KL_mbx_evt.sv:28-45,108,155,342,387` (coalescing; a LINK record posts only when the level differs from `posted_up_r`), `sw/firmware/ctrl/srp/README.md`, `sw/firmware/ctrl/loop/ctrl_loop.h`, and `docs/design/REBOOT_RESET.md` (REBOOT is an IPROG reload).
- The diff and per-commit history.
- The author's public packet at `62593bf0:review-evidence/973-r1/author-r1`.
- The hosted runs at the exact head.

Frozen acceptance (#973):
- (a) On the one-hart image, a link-up at any phase of a pass resets SRP's interface once, with the startup participants kept.
- (b) The host test of that ordering fails before the fix and passes after, at 1x1/1if and 8x8/1if, with a planted defect.
- (c) The CPU budget rows are unchanged within their bounds.
- (d) The images are within their ledgers.

The author reads (a) as two cases: a first UP resets nothing and keeps the startup participants (`on_event`, `hold`), and a later UP resets once. I accept that reading. It is what `on_event`'s first-UP rule (`srp_mbx.c:1227-1230`) already defines.

Independence note: I completed my pass over the diff before reading any PR comments. While listing the PR's comments to look for prior findings, I saw the heading and first lines of a concurrent external reviewer's comment. I stopped reading it there. My findings and ledger do not derive from it. The only earlier public rounds on this PR are the two review-start notices, so no prior finding needs resolving or retaining.

## Findings

### R895-1-F1 BLOCKER - lenses: Tests, Docs - `sw/firmware/ctrl/test/ctrl_configs.py:156` (`OUTSIDE`) with `sw/firmware/ctrl/test/srp_link_mutants.py:8` - the new plant table is not classified by the firmware boundary gate; hosted `firmware-boundary` fails at this head

- **Requirement/evidence:**
  - `ctrl_configs.held()` refuses any file that names the firmware's tree and compiles nothing, unless it is a known builder or is listed in `PART_OF`, `OUTSIDE` or `SUITES` (`ctrl_configs.py:441-466`). `srp_link_mutants.py` names `sw/firmware/ctrl` in its docstring (line 8) and is in none of those lists.
  - Its sibling tables are in `OUTSIDE` with a reason: `srp_talker_mutants.py`, `srp_listener_mutants.py` and `srp_reclaim_mutants.py` (`ctrl_configs.py:173-179`).
  - Hosted rtl-fast run 45061747278, job `firmware-boundary`, on head `9a71daa9`, failed at 19:58:17Z with: `REFUSED: sw/firmware/ctrl/test/srp_link_mutants.py names the firmware's tree, compiled nothing in the capture, and is neither a known builder (ctrl_configs.BUILDERS), one whose compiles are none of the firmware's (OUTSIDE), nor one that compiles only in a suite (SUITES)`, exit 2 (`receipts/hosted/firmware-boundary-failed-step.txt`).
  - The fail-fast then cancelled the rest of rtl-fast (`firmware-srp-mutants`, `firmware-control-mutants`, `publication-census`, `yosys-elaboration`). It also cancelled all nineteen rtl-full Verilator shards, which is why `verilator-suites` and `yosys-portability` fail (`receipts/hosted/runs-at-head.txt`).
  - My static census (`scripts/boundary_census.py`, `receipts/boundary-census-head.txt`) lists `srp_link_mutants.py` among the text-found builders that no list classifies. It is the only one of them that compiles nothing.
  - The documented local firmware gate set includes `ctrl_boundary.py --require-rv32 --selftest` (`docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md:3629`). It appears in neither the TAKEN validation plan nor the REVIEW READY evidence. The PR's Status still says "GREEN".
- **Impact:** the head cannot get a successful `rtl-fast` verdict, which is a completion bullet in AGENTS section 7. The fail-fast leaves this head without SRP-mutant and rtl-full hosted evidence. The published readiness claim is wrong about the head.
- **Required change:** `ctrl_boundary.py --require-rv32 --selftest` passes at the new head, with the new table classified as its siblings are. The local receipt for that gate is published. The PR's Status and evidence state the gate.
- **Verification:** `boundary_census.py` no longer lists `srp_link_mutants.py`. A local `ctrl_boundary.py --require-rv32 --selftest` exits 0. Hosted `firmware-boundary` succeeds at the new head, and the cancelled jobs then execute.

### R895-1-F2 MINOR - lenses: Conformance, RTL, Robustness, Tests, Docs - `sw/firmware/ctrl/srp/srp_mbx.c:1474` with `:1286`; `sw/firmware/ctrl/srp/README.md:111-113` - after a re-attach that reads a DOWN whose record the fabric then elides, SRP never follows the link that is up

- **Requirement/evidence:**
  - At head, `srp_mbx_attach` sets `link_carried` to the register level it reads (line 1474). The poll takes an UP only while `link_carried` is set (line 1286).
  - The fabric posts a LINK record only when the level differs from the last level it posted (`KL_mbx_evt.sv:155,387`; `mbx_model.c:169`). So a DOWN that is held by a full ring and then recovers before posting yields no record. The README states this case itself: "A held DOWN record can disappear when the level recovers" (line 113).
  - Sequence: SRP is destroyed and re-initialized after its loop has consumed the UP record. While the link is momentarily down with its DOWN record held, attach reads DOWN, so `link_carried` is false. The level recovers, and no record is owed. From then on, no LINK ever sets `link_carried`, so SRP holds the interface down on an up link indefinitely, until the next real link change.
  - At base, the poll took the register's UP and recovered. README line 112 states that contract: "Polling reconciles that level even without another LINK record". At head that statement is false in this case.
  - Executable evidence: `scripts/probe_reattach_elided.cpp` is a disposable suite on the repository's own fixture, modelled on `Srp.CancelledLinkRecordRecoversFromLevelAndFencesOldReceive` (`srp_mbx.cpp:1062`) and `Srp.ReattachLearnsAnAlreadyUpLinkWithoutAnotherRecord` (`:1035`).
    - At head, `Srp.ProbeReattachWhileItsDownRecordIsElided` FAILS at 1x1/1if and 8x8/1if: "PROBE: SRP does not follow a link that is up" (`receipts/probe-reattach-head.log`).
    - On the base firmware, the same suite PASSES at both shapes (`receipts/probe-reattach-basefw.log`).
    - The control case, a re-attach with the link down followed by an owed UP, passes on both.
  - Not covered elsewhere: none of the seven plants or the tests exercises a re-attach that reads DOWN. The PR's limitations list the dropped-UP-on-re-entry case but not this one.
- **Reachability:** not on the shipping image's boot path. `ctrl_plat.c:405` attaches SRP once after a full fabric reset (REBOOT is an IPROG reload, `docs/design/REBOOT_RESET.md:27-34`). The fabric posts the first UP after reset, and that record is still in the ring when SRP attaches, so it sets `link_carried`. The exposure is the documented re-attach API (`README.md:110-111`; exercised by the tests) and any future runtime re-attach. That is why this is MINOR, not MAJOR.
- **Lenses:**
  - Conformance: in that path, an operational port carries no MRP declarations (IEEE 802.1Q-2018 10.7, the behaviour #973 cites).
  - RTL: the adapter's documented attach and poll contract no longer holds.
  - Robustness: re-attach during a link transition, an ordering and reset path.
  - Tests: no test or plant covers it.
  - Docs: README line 112 is false, and the PR omits the limitation.
- **Required change:** one of the following, without reintroducing #973's double reset (my plant `rv-poll-resets-on-register-up` and the author's `link-pass-attach-carries-an-up` must stay killed):
  - SRP follows an up link after a re-attach that read DOWN when no LINK record is owed; or
  - the limitation is stated exactly in the adapter README (line 112 corrected), pinned by a test, and filed as a follow-up Issue, as AGENTS section 4 requires for new work.
- **Verification:** the probe passes at the new head; or the README states the case and a committed test asserts the documented behaviour. In both cases the existing link-pass suite and the twelve plants stay green and killed.

### R895-1-F3 SUGGESTION - lens: Robustness - `sw/firmware/ctrl/srp/srp_mbx.c:1286` with `:1227-1229` - a DOWN inside a pass still resets twice

The poll resets on the register's DOWN, and the LINK DOWN record resets again. The second reset normally comes before any rebuild, which I confirmed by reading `reset_interface` (`reopen_polls = 1`). If the ring holds the DOWN record for more than one pass, the participants are rebuilt while the link is down and then destroyed again. Nothing is transmitted, because `i->link` is false. This is pre-existing and disclosed in the PR's limitations, and #973's acceptance is the link-up. Suggest a follow-up Issue if the wasted rebuild matters for the CPU budget.

### R895-1-F4 SUGGESTION - lenses: Robustness, Docs - `sw/firmware/ctrl/srp/srp_mbx.c:61-71` (`enter`) with `:1286` - an UP that the sink drops on re-entry is no longer recovered from the register

This path is counted and asserted in debug builds, so it is an invariant violation, not an expected path. The PR body discloses it. Suggest stating it in the adapter README beside the new rule, so the README is the complete statement of when SRP follows the register.

### R895-1-F5 RESIDUE - PR #978 body, "Linked Issue / roles" - the related-issue list omits issues the task names

The issue relates to #665, #970 and #972, and the PR's limitations name #872. The PR body's line reads `Relates to #665`. Exact fix: `Relates to #665, #970, #972, #872`.

## What was checked against the focus list

1. **Cause on the one-hart split image (IEEE 802.1Q-2018 10.7, 35.2):** confirmed.
   - The loop dispatches the ring's records at a pass's start (`ctrl_loop.c` `service_events`; `ctrl_loop.h` pass order), and SRP's poll read the register later (`dd163e41:srp_mbx.c` poll, `links[n] = mbx_link_up(n)`).
   - `srp_link_pass.cpp` on the base firmware (head tests, base `srp_mbx.c/.h`) fails only `SrpLinkPass.AfterTheEventsBeforeSrpsPoll`, at 1x1/1if, 8x8/1if, 8x8/2if and 1x1/2if. The other three phases pass. The diagnostics: "SRP's poll took a level no LINK had carried"; resets 2, not 0; "a first UP keeps the startup participants" (`receipts/basefw-arms.log`).
   - At head, all four tests pass at the same four shapes (`receipts/head-arms.log`).
2. **The fix:**
   - `link_carried` is set only by SRP's own LINK sink (`srp_mbx.c:1233`) and by attach (`:1474`).

## New finding

### R896-2-F1 BLOCKER - Conformance, RTL, Robustness, Tests, Docs - stale uncarried-UP mark authorizes a different UP

**Artifacts:** `sw/firmware/ctrl/srp/srp_mbx.c:1285` and `:1303`; `sw/firmware/ctrl/test/srp_link_pass.cpp:142`; `sw/firmware/ctrl/srp/README.md:117`; `probe_stale_mark.cpp`; `endstation_ax7101_1x1_tdm8.log` and `endstation_ax7101_8x8.log`.

**Authority/evidence:** #973's first-UP/startup-preservation acceptance and the documented register/event ordering. The poll short-circuits `carried_up` when the register reads DOWN. Consequently bit 1 of `link_carried`, set for an earlier uncarried UP, survives that DOWN. A later UP can promote the old mark to bit 0 using an empty-ring observation that preceded the *new* UP.

The executable sequence uses the committed fixture, normal event posting and the committed full-ring stimulus. It neither writes `link_carried` nor pauses the event poster:

1. Start with link DOWN and clean startup participants. Fill the event ring with counter-change events.
2. Raise UP after a pass's event take. The ring is still full, so no UP record posts. The poll marks the uncarried UP (`link_carried = 2`).
3. Return DOWN before any take frees space. The fabric's last posted level is already DOWN, so the pending UP disappears. Drain the ring while DOWN. No LINK record clears the mark, and the raw-DOWN short circuit leaves it set.
4. Raise a fresh UP after a later pass's event take. That pass observed an empty ring before the fresh UP. The poll promotes the stale mark and resets immediately, before the new LINK is dispatched.
5. The next dispatched UP sees `link_seen` and resets again.

`KL_mbx_evt.sv:155` selects LINK only when its level differs from `posted_up_r`; `:387` records the level when posting starts. `ctrl_loop.c:144` takes events before the polls, and `:158` records whether it exhausted its eight-record allowance. The host model's `next_source` and full-ring behavior match those relevant rules. The failure needs an ordinary coalesced transient, not re-attach or illegal re-entry.

At both shipping shapes, the new test observes two resets instead of zero, premature `link_seen`, and a changed participant pointer. All seven committed phase/full-ring/re-attach tests pass in the same binaries. With only production `srp_mbx.c/.h` restored from `9a71daa9` into a disposable source copy, the identical new test passes at both shapes. This establishes a regression in this delta, not an inherited defect or a failing setup.

**Impact:** the shipping SRP lifecycle again exhibits the double reset and startup-participant loss #973 is intended to remove. The new comment/README argument establishes that an old owed event has been handled or elided; it does not establish that a fresh UP occurring after the latest event take has no event outstanding. The first-UP claim is therefore false for this supported ordering, which is substantive documentation failure rather than wording residue.

**Required outcome:** an observation associated with an earlier uncarried UP must not authorize a fresh UP after an intervening DOWN. Preserve re-attach/elided-DOWN recovery, immediate fail-closed DOWN, the ordinary carried-UP recovery behavior, and the first/later-UP reset rules. Add a committed regression and an effective plant for this sequence; make the lifecycle explanation account for the observation's validity. No particular implementation is prescribed.

**Verification:** the supplied new probe passes at both shipping shapes with zero first-UP resets and unchanged startup participants; all existing seven link tests and the original re-attach probe remain green; `rv-poll-resets-on-register-up`, `link-pass-attach-carries-an-up` and the updated link plants remain killed. Recheck image ledgers and applicable CPU evidence after the production fix, given the eight-byte ROM headroom.

**Lens attribution:** Conformance: frozen acceptance fails. RTL: adapter state and event-poster/loop ordering are inconsistent. Robustness: an elided transient followed by a new edge triggers it. Tests: the committed full-ring test covers an UP that stays UP, but misses its elision and replacement. Docs: the new recovery argument and first-UP guarantee omit this case.
